title: The last lighthouse keepers
summary_es: Los últimos fareros. Relativos, estructuras de énfasis y de concesión, y adverbios poco frecuentes.
text: There was a time {{1}} every lighthouse on the coast had a keeper, someone {{2}} job it was to climb the stairs each evening and light the lamp. Automation has long {{3}} made the profession obsolete, and today {{4}} a handful of keepers remain anywhere in the world. Those who do are employed {{5}} so much to operate the light as to maintain the buildings and welcome visitors. {{6}} lonely the work may sound, former keepers rarely describe it that way. Many speak instead of a sense of purpose that they have never found in {{7}} other job. One retired keeper told me that he had not {{8}} missed the mainland during his thirty years on a rock in the Atlantic.

gaps.explanation_es: «There was a time when…» = hubo un tiempo en que… Relativo de tiempo.
«Someone whose job it was to…» = alguien cuyo trabajo consistía en… Estructura formal muy frecuente en C1.
«Has long since» + participio = hace ya mucho que. «Ago» no puede ir con present perfect.
«Only a handful of» = apenas un puñado de.
«Not so much to… as to…» = no tanto para… como para… Estructura de contraste.
«However + adjetivo + sujeto + may» = por muy… que… Concesión.
Tras un verbo en negativa (never) va «any»: in any other job.
«Not once» = ni una sola vez. Refuerza la negación.
